title: P15 Session 2 - Medication Near-Miss Root Cause Analysis
goal: Conduct a root-cause analysis (RCA) of a wrong-time medication near-miss: build a scenario and timestamped timeline, map contributing factors into a fishbone diagram, drill down with five-whys to a systemic root cause, draft an illustrated corrective action plan, and synthesize everything into a one-page safety committee report.

Step 1.step_name: Write a medication near-miss scenario and generate a timestamped incident timeline.
Step 1.step_action: Write a medication near-miss patient scenario involving one patient from Session 1 and generate a timeline of events leading up to the near-miss incident.

nodes.label: Define RCA task scope and upload source data
nodes.detail: User composes one long combined prompt asking Claude to build a full medication-error RCA (fishbone diagram, five-whys, corrective action plan) and to write a wrong-time medication near-miss scenario grounded in Session 1's nursing assignment and patient census, attaching both spreadsheet files.

nodes.label: Review source data and build near-miss incident analysis
nodes.detail: Reviews the nursing-assignment and patient-acuity spreadsheets, using RN-4's reduced assignment and Room 108's clinical event to ground the scenario. Develops the near-miss scenario around RN-4 being pulled into a rapid response and a time-critical antibiotic being missed, then builds the timestamped incident timeline and analysis document, rendering the output to verify formatting before delivery.

nodes.label: Review and confirm scenario and timeline
nodes.detail: User reads the delivered "Rca wrong time med error" document and confirms the timeline holds together and reads correctly before moving on to the fishbone step.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: accept the rca wrong time med error doc

Step 2.step_name: Map contributing factors into a fishbone diagram.
Step 2.step_action: Claude will build a fishbone diagram from the timeline while sorting contributing factors into categories of people, processes, communication, environment, and equipment. Claude to recheck work if work does not show enough output.

nodes.label: Request fishbone categorization of contributing factors
nodes.detail: User asks Claude to sort contributing factors into People/Process/Communication/Environment/Equipment and explicitly requests a real SVG fishbone/Ishikawa diagram artifact rather than a chat table.

nodes.label: Build initial Ishikawa fishbone diagram
nodes.detail: Claude designs a color-coded fishbone SVG with category spines and specific factors branching off each (e.g. RN-4 sole responder, verbal-only reassignment, eMAR alert routing), fixing an invalid XML comment bug before rendering and delivering the first version.

nodes.label: Review the initial Ishikawa fishbone diagram and supporting explanation
nodes.detail: The participant reads Claude's explanation of how the contributing factors were remapped into the five categories and looks at the first fishbone diagram.

nodes.label: Request diagram condensed to one printable page
nodes.detail: User reports the first fishbone is too large and condensed to read, and asks for a version that fits on one page.

nodes.label: Revise fishbone into a compact one-page layout
nodes.detail: Claude rebuilds the diagram at a tighter US Letter landscape aspect ratio, fixes a font-rendering artifact, and trims whitespace until it fits comfortably on one page.

nodes.label: View the in-progress fishbone render while Claude condenses it
nodes.detail: While Claude rebuilds the fishbone to fit one page, the participant enlarges the intermediate render Claude shows mid-run to look at the layout.

nodes.label: Review the revised one-page fishbone diagram and analysis document
nodes.detail: The participant reads Claude's notes on the condensed 1056x660 layout and checks the revised one-page fishbone diagram.

nodes.label: Request verification that every factor traces to the timeline
nodes.detail: User asks Claude to ensure every contributing factor on the fishbone traces back to something specific in the incident timeline.

nodes.label: Audit fishbone factors against timeline and flag unsupported claims
nodes.detail: Claude cross-checks each factor against the timeline in a Factor/Anchor/Traceable table, flags several inferred (not explicitly logged) factors as not-traceable, and catches and removes one invented claim that contradicted the timeline, delivering an annotated fishbone with a filled/open-dot legend.

nodes.label: Review the timeline-traceability audit and flagged unsupported factors
nodes.detail: The participant reads the factor-to-timeline audit, in which Claude cites the timestamp each factor traces to and flags factors that are not explicitly logged in the timeline.

nodes.label: Direct Claude to treat discretionary/inferred actions as legitimate and recheck
nodes.detail: User instructs Claude not to discard reasonably inferred, discretionary or emergency-driven factors, and to recheck the factor-to-timeline mapping again under that guidance.

nodes.label: Finalize fishbone diagram with corrected factor classification
nodes.detail: Claude reclassifies factors per the new guidance, self-corrects a factual timestamp error (Room 115's stable/discharge status was logged at 0600, not 0700), and delivers the finalized, legend-annotated fishbone SVG.

nodes.label: Review the finalized fishbone diagram and corrected factor classifications
nodes.detail: With the final fishbone SVG open in the side panel, the participant reads aloud Claude's explanation of the filled-dot (logged event) versus open-dot (inferred) markings and the corrected Room 115 timestamp.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: accept the fishbone diagram after refinement

Step 3.step_name: Five-whys drill-down on the top contributing factor.
Step 3.step_action: Claude to find the single most significant contributing factor and work through five successive 'why' questions to reach a systemic root-cause rather than stopping at human error.

nodes.label: Request five-whys drill-down on the top fishbone factor
nodes.detail: User asks Claude to identify the single most significant contributing factor from the fishbone by causal weight and build a five-whys drill-down artifact from it.

nodes.label: Select top factor and build five-whys drill-down artifact
nodes.detail: Claude selects the Equipment branch (eMAR alert routed only to RN-4's now-unattended device) as the strongest, most evidentially-anchored factor and builds a color-coded five-whys SVG walking from Why 1 (alert misrouting) to the Why 5 root cause (no workflow step reassigns a responding nurse's other time-critical medication tasks), fixing a text-overflow bug before delivering.

nodes.label: Review the five-whys drill-down artifact and selected top factor
nodes.detail: The participant reads Claude's reasoning for choosing the Equipment branch as the top factor and looks through the five-whys drill-down artifact.

nodes.label: Request recheck for alternative, more logical RCA chains
nodes.detail: User asks Claude to recheck all prior work to make sure no other RCA starting point is more logical than the Equipment chain it built.

nodes.label: Stress-test alternative causal chains against the timeline
nodes.detail: Claude tests a People-first chain (rejected as a clinical trigger, not a controllable root cause) and a Communication-first chain (an equally legitimate parallel path converging on the same root cause) plus a weaker Process-first chain, keeps Equipment as primary, and adds a disclosure box noting the valid parallel Communication path.

nodes.label: Review the alternative causal-chain stress test and primary-factor conclusion
nodes.detail: The participant reads Claude's stress test of the People-first, Communication-first, and Process-first chains and its conclusion that the Equipment chain remains the primary one.

nodes.label: Request five-whys artifact resized to fit one printable page
nodes.detail: User asks Claude to ensure the five-whys SVG fits on a single US Letter page.

nodes.label: Resize and finalize five-whys artifact for print
nodes.detail: Claude rebuilds the diagram at Letter-portrait dimensions with compressed vertical spacing, trims excess whitespace, and delivers the final one-page five-whys artifact.

nodes.label: Review the finalized one-page five-whys artifact
nodes.detail: The participant looks at the resized one-page (Letter portrait) five-whys artifact.

Step 4.step_name: Draft a corrective action plan and illustrate it.
Step 4.step_action: Generate 3 corrective actions to address the root cause from step 3, each with owner, timeframe, and a way to measure success.

nodes.label: Request corrective action plan with three fixes tied to the RCA
nodes.detail: User asks Claude to build a corrective-action-plan document with three fixes addressing the root cause, each with an owner, timeframe, and measure of success, explicitly cross-referencing both the five-whys and fishbone artifacts.

nodes.label: Draft and verify three-fix corrective action plan document
nodes.detail: Claude cross-references both artifacts to propose three ordered fixes (eMAR reconfiguration, structured handoff checklist, dedicated charge-relief coverage), builds a DOCX with a fix-to-RCA traceability table, and works through a stale-cache PDF rendering bug before confirming a clean two-page document.

nodes.label: Review the corrective action plan and RCA traceability
nodes.detail: The participant reads Claude's fix-to-RCA traceability table and opens the corrective action plan document to review the three fixes with their owners, timeframes, and measures of success.

nodes.label: Check the corrective action plan document and request an illustration mapping the fixes to the root cause
nodes.detail: After reviewing the plan, user asks Claude to add an illustration showing how the three fixes map back to the root cause.

nodes.label: Build fix-to-root-cause box diagram illustration
nodes.detail: Claude designs a diagram with the root cause at the center and each fix branching from it, rasterizes it, and embeds it into the corrective-action-plan docx, verifying placement across pages.

nodes.label: Review the fix-to-root-cause box diagram
nodes.detail: The participant enlarges the new fix-to-root-cause box diagram (root cause in the middle, fixes branching from it) and comments on how it looks.

nodes.label: Reject box diagram as too "PowerPoint-y", request a storyline illustration
nodes.detail: User asks Claude to replace the diagram with a narrative storyline illustration instead.

nodes.label: Rebuild illustration as a four-scene horizontal storyline
nodes.detail: Claude designs a narrative scene-based illustration walking through the incident moment and the fixes, and swaps it into the docx, verifying page placement.

nodes.label: View the in-progress storyline render while Claude rebuilds it
nodes.detail: While Claude builds the four-scene storyline illustration, the participant enlarges the intermediate render Claude shows mid-run.

nodes.label: Request illustration reformatted as comic-strip panels
nodes.detail: User asks Claude to make each scene fit half a page and look more like a comic strip.

nodes.label: Rebuild illustration as a 2x2 comic-panel grid
nodes.detail: Claude rebuilds the illustration as a true comic strip with panel borders, gutters, speech bubbles and motion lines, fixing a Panel-1 overlap issue before embedding it in the docx.

nodes.label: View the corrective action plan document while Claude rebuilds the comic
nodes.detail: While Claude rebuilds the illustration as a 2x2 comic grid, the participant scrolls through the corrective action plan document in Claude's side panel and looks at the intermediate comic render.

nodes.label: Review the response about revised 2×2 comic-panel illustration
nodes.detail: The participant reads Claude's summary of the 2x2 comic-panel rebuild and looks at the new comic illustration.

nodes.label: Request more realistic nurse figures and proper comic speech bubbles
nodes.detail: User asks Claude to redo the comic strip with real comic-style speech bubbles and more realistic nurse figures and medical iconography instead of blob-people.

nodes.label: Rebuild nurse figures and speech bubbles via Python-generated SVG
nodes.detail: After discovering cairosvg does not support CSS custom properties, Claude writes a Python helper generating realistic nurse figures with distinguishing scrub colors, and fixes a floating-head layout bug and speech-bubble/caption overlaps across several render-check-edit cycles before embedding the corrected illustration.

nodes.label: View in-progress comic renders while Claude rebuilds the nurse figures
nodes.detail: While Claude rewrites the nurse figures and speech bubbles over several passes, the participant enlarges the intermediate comic renders Claude shows mid-run.

nodes.label: Review the corrected nurse-figure illustration and updated corrective action plan
nodes.detail: The participant reads Claude's summary of the speech-bubble and nurse-figure fixes and looks at the updated comic panels in the corrective action plan.

nodes.label: Flag a three-armed nurse figure bug in Panel 3
nodes.detail: User notices and reports that Panel 3's nurse figure appears to have three arms.

nodes.label: Fix Panel-3 arm-rendering bug and finalize illustration
nodes.detail: Claude adds an option to the nurse-figure generator to suppress the default arm so Panel 3's RN-5 no longer shows a duplicate arm, confirms all four panels render cleanly, and rebuilds the final docx.

nodes.label: Review the finalized illustration and corrected Panel 3 rendering
nodes.detail: The participant scrolls through the final corrective action plan document in Claude's side panel, including the fixed comic illustration, the corrective actions, and the committee notes.

Step 5.step_name: Generate and proofread a one-page safety committee report.
Step 5.step_action: Synthesize steps 1 to 4 in a one-page summary for the unit safety committee with the incident summary, contributing factors, root cause, and corrective action plan.

nodes.label: Request one-page safety committee report synthesizing all steps
nodes.detail: User asks Claude to prepare a one-page safety committee report summarizing the incident, contributing factors, root cause, and corrective action plan from all prior steps.

nodes.label: Build one-page safety committee summary document
nodes.detail: Claude pulls confirmed facts from the RCA timeline, fishbone artifact, five-whys artifact, and corrective action plan into a single-page DOCX with an incident summary, key contributing factors table, root cause statement, and the three-fix corrective action table, verifying it fits one page.

nodes.label: Review the one-page safety committee summary document
nodes.detail: The participant reads Claude's summary of the one-page safety committee report and opens the document to review it.

nodes.label: Request proofreading and formatting changes to the summary
nodes.detail: User reviews the summary and asks Claude to check it for typos/grammar, enlarge the closing summary sentences to a readable bold-italic size, and highlight/enlarge the root cause text.

nodes.label: Proofread document and apply requested formatting
nodes.detail: Claude proofreads and finds no actual grammar errors (tightening one slightly wordy sentence), then boxes the root cause in red highlighted bold text, bolds/italicizes the measure-of-success values, and enlarges/bolds/italicizes the closing summary in navy, confirming it still fits one page; the video ends immediately after this final version is delivered.

nodes.label: Review the finalized and reformatted safety committee summary
nodes.detail: The participant reads Claude's proofreading result and looks at the reformatted one-page summary with the boxed root cause and enlarged closing summary.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: accept the one page safety committee summary
